paragraphs.text: DSH plugin: trims thinking content, repeated reads, terminal inputs, and middle turns from the model
request, while the local session log stays complete.
# dsh-context-saver · DSH context saving plugin
A send-time context trimmer for DeepSeek Harness.
It trims only at the moment the context is submitted to the model. The local session log, the chat t
ranscript, and the trajectory view stay complete. With the plugin disabled, or with every option off
, the request is byte-identical to the untrimmed one.
English | 中文
## What it is for
What makes a long session expensive is not the number of turns, it is that every turn re-sends the s
long session expensive is not the number of turns, it is that every turn re-sends the same material:

- the model's own thinking is passed back on every request and grows monotonically;
- the same file

or page is read again and again, so its content appears three or five times;
- a terminal command's

full argument text is passed back every turn, while only its output matters;
- turns from long ago s
till occupy the window although they no longer inform the current decision.
This plugin removes that material from the **outbound copy** only; the local copy keeps everything.
## How it works
Every model request in DSH passes through the `llm/stream` waterfall, which carries the complete `me
ssages` about to be submitted.
The plugin takes the request there, builds a new message array from the enabled rules, and re-dispat
ches it with `ctx.llm.stream()`. The original request is deep-frozen and is never modified, and no s
ession event is ever written, so:

- the local session log, `session/event`, the trajectory view, and exports keep the full history;
-

every request recomputes the trimmed copy from the complete local record;
- trimming is **determinis
tic** — the same input always produces the same output — so the common prefix of two consecutive req
uests stays byte-identical and the KV cache hit rate is essentially unaffected.
### Why the result cannot make DeepSeek reject the request
The DeepSeek Messages adapter imposes hard structural rules. Every shape this plugin emits was desig
ned around them and verified against the live API:
| Risk | Handling | Verified |
| a `tool_result` without its `tool_use` | `tool-call` blocks are **never removed**, only `arguments

` becomes `{}` | accepted |
| a `tool_use` without an immediate result | `tool` role messages are **

never removed**, only their content is emptied | accepted |
| thinking block count out of step with
local replay metadata | `reasoning` blocks are **never removed**, only `text` is emptied and the sig

nature kept | accepted |
| an empty thinking block rejected | the real signature is still sent | acc
epted (empty + signature, empty without signature, and no thinking block all return 200) |
Compaction and session-title requests (`purpose` set) are never trimmed, so their own input cannot c
hange underneath them.
## Interface
The control sits in the composer tool row, next to the model and sandbox selectors. Clicking it open
the composer tool row, next to the model and sandbox selectors. Clicking it opens a floating panel:

- **Master switch** (on by default)
- **Strip thinking content** (on by default) — keeps each think

block, empties its text, so the model receives the answer without the reasoning
- **Strip repeated r
eads** (on by default) — identical file and page reads keep only the first copy; later ones keep an

identifier and an empty structure
- **Strip terminal inputs and process** (off by default) — termina

l tool calls keep their output and lose the model-supplied arguments
- **Strip the middle of the con
text** (off by default) — turning it on raises a warning: *"Stripping the middle of the context can

remove important content from the middle of a long conversation while it is being sent!"*
- **Leadin

g turns kept** (5 by default, effective only with middle stripping on)
- **Trailing turns kept** (5
by default, effective only with middle stripping on)
The panel is localized in Chinese and English and follows the DSH language setting. Settings are sto
red on this machine and apply to every session:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The switch track uses a fixed mid-green (on, `#22c55e`) and neutral grey (off, `#9aa0a6`) rather tha
n the theme's `brand-primary` / `border-l2`: in the dark theme those two aliases resolve to a near-w
hite `#f9fafb` and a translucent white, so a white knob on them shows no visible state.
## Middle stripping rule
**One turn is one user message plus the model output that follows it**, so turn boundaries are the `
ne user message plus the model output that follows it**, so turn boundaries are the `user` messages.
With `N` turns in total, `H` leading turns kept, and `T` trailing turns kept:

- when `N ≤ H + T` nothing is stripped at all (the two retention windows overlap);
- otherwise a tur
n is stripped only when it is inside neither window. A stripped turn keeps its structure and loses i
ts content: tool calls keep their id and name with empty arguments, reasoning blocks keep their posi
tion and signature with empty text, text and images are cleared, so tool calls and results stay pair
n and signature with empty text, text and images are cleared, so tool calls and results stay paired.
Example: 17 turns, 7 leading, 8 trailing → turns 1–7 and 10–17 are kept and turns 8 and 9 are stripp
ed (`7 + 8 = 15` turns retained).
> At least one turn is always kept at each end. The trailing turn carries the current question — emp
tying it would send a request with no question in it — and the leading one keeps the request startin
g on a user message. A configured `0` is raised to `1`.
## Measured on real sessions
Two independent measurements, both against the live `deepseek-flash` endpoint.
**A real 65-turn session log from this machine**, replayed through the adapter's own serialization r
ules with the session's own 34 tool declarations:
| | Prompt tokens | Reply |

| Untrimmed | 867,787 | accepted |
| **Trimmed (defaults)** | **574,347** | accepted |
33.8% fewer prompt tokens on a long agentic session, and the model still answered correctly.
**A 60-turn synthetic session with heavy repeated reads**, comparing the request for turn N against
the request for turn N+1 to measure prefix reuse:
| Configuration | Prompt tokens | Cache hit rate |

| Trimming off | 21,102 | 98.9% |
